# Opposed Minkowski flow: exact cap calculus and an actual interior minimum

This note concerns the actual three integer fibers at bases -1,0,1.
It supplies exact planar cap variations for the opposed Minkowski flow,
including the moving cap boundary and its complementary cap. It also
gives an exact strict interior minimum of the full normalized maximum
depth along that flow. The minimum is above 2/9. No below-target
extremizer, or exclusion of one, is inferred from this example.

The equal-endpoint-area subclass already satisfies the target by
`candidate 9dc053aa681e5ef6`, Corollary 3. Consequently the
new variation statements below allow unequal endpoint areas.

## 1. Actual family, exact total mass, and admissible parameter range

Let A,C be full-dimensional compact convex planar bodies, and set

    B=(A+C)/2,
    A_s=(1-s)A+sC, C_s=sA+(1-s)C, 0<=s<=1.

Minkowski addition gives exactly (A_s+C_s)/2=B. Therefore

    Q_s=conv({-1}xA_s union {0}xB union {1}xC_s)

is a full-dimensional compact convex body whose only integer fibers
are exactly A_s,B,C_s. No new midpoint containment error is introduced.
In fact the middle lift is redundant in the convex hull. Every interior
parameter permits both signs of a sufficiently small change in s.

Write a=|A|, c=|C|, q=V(A,C) for mixed area, and W=|B|. Then

    |A_s|=(1-s)^2 a+2s(1-s)q+s^2 c,
    |C_s|=s^2 a+2s(1-s)q+(1-s)^2 c,
    W=(a+c+2q)/4.

With Delta=2q-a-c=4W-2(a+c), the exact mixed mass is

    M_s=a+c+W+2 Delta s(1-s),
    M_s'=2 Delta(1-2s), M_s''=-4 Delta,                 (1)
    |A_s|-|C_s|=(1-2s)(a-c).

For a=c=V, Delta=4(W-V)>=0; its vanishing forces A,C
to be translates by the equality case of planar Brunn--Minkowski.
For unequal areas Delta can be negative even for homothetic bodies.
Thus opposed interpolation does not generally increase total mass.

## 2. Exact polynomial cap calculus for arbitrary polygons

Suppose now A,C are convex polygons. Fix a nonzero continuous normal u,
an integer anchor j in {-1,0,1}, an affine continuous threshold t(s),
and an initial base tilt beta. Continue the actual ambient halfspace as

    H_s={u.x+(1-2s) beta(z-j)>=t(s)}.

Its threshold in fiber z is

    q_z(s)=t(s)-(1-2s)beta(z-j),
    q_z'=t'+2 beta(z-j).                               (2)

If t(s)=u.y(s), it passes through the actual candidate (j,y(s))
whenever y(s) belongs to that fiber. In particular j=0 and a fixed
y in B give a fixed middle candidate for the entire flow.

For 0<s<1, A_s and C_s have the common refinement of the normal fans
of A and C. Their support numbers are affine functions of s. Every
vertex, obtained by intersecting two adjacent fixed support lines, is
therefore affine in s. Every intersection of an edge support line with
the moving cap line u.x=q_z(s) is also affine, provided the lines are
not parallel. A parallel line either misses that edge or coincides
with it; coincident events are treated by one-sided chambers below.

There are only finitely many isolated parameter events: a moving cap
line hits a vertex when a nonidentically-zero affine incidence function
vanishes. An identically zero incidence means that the cap line passes
through that moving vertex throughout the interval; the vertex simply
remains in the fixed clipped vertex list. Such a cap may be proper.
Between the isolated events the clipped polygon has a fixed cyclic
vertex list v_i(s)=p_i+s w_i. Its
area F_z(s) is exactly quadratic, with

    F_z(s)=1/2 sum_i det(v_i(s),v_(i+1)(s)),
    F_z'=1/2 sum_i [det(w_i,v_(i+1))+det(v_i,w_(i+1))],
    F_z''=sum_i det(w_i,w_(i+1)).                       (3)

Empty and full caps are included as the corresponding empty or full
polygon lists. A cap-line/EDGE-line coincidence persisting throughout
an interval is a supporting cap with area zero, or its full-area
complement. This supporting conclusion is not asserted for persistent
vertex incidence. Thus the
entire full ambient cap mass F(s)=F_-(s)+F_0(s)+F_+(s) has an exact
piecewise-quadratic description. There is no omitted family of oblique
normals or assumption that cap mass is bounded above by cap
Brunn--Minkowski.

Here is the boundary-flux form of the same first derivative. Let n_i
be the fixed unit outward edge normals in the common fan, and put

    d_i=h_C(n_i)-h_A(n_i).

Let L_zi(s) be the length of the part of edge i of fiber z in H_s,
and let ell_z(s) be the length of its chord on u.x=q_z(s). On every
proper-cut chamber,

    F'(s)=sum_i d_i[L_-i(s)-L_+i(s)]
                         -sum_(z=-1)^1 q_z' ell_z(s)/|u|,
    F''(s)=sum_i d_i[L_-'i(s)-L_+'i(s)]
                         -sum_(z=-1)^1 q_z' ell_z'(s)/|u|.   (4)

The edge velocities are d_i,-d_i,0 in A_s,C_s,B respectively.
The last sums are the moving-cap-boundary contributions, not shape
terms. All the chord lengths and captured edge lengths in (4) are
affine within the chamber, as also follows from the fixed-line
intersection description. For a fixed middle candidate, (4) becomes

    F'=sum_i d_i(L_-i-L_+i)+2 beta(ell_--ell_+)/|u|.    (5)

The cap of B is then constant. Formula (4), rather than (5), must be
used for a candidate on an endpoint or a moving continuous center.

Planar area assigns zero mass to every line. Consequently the closed
complementary cap F^c(s), with the reverse inequality, satisfies exactly

    F(s)+F^c(s)=M_s,
    F'+(F^c)'=M_s', F''+(F^c)''=M_s''                 (6)

on every chamber and with the respective one-sided derivatives at
events. These identities include the middle cap and all endpoint mass.

A supporting-edge event can have a genuine first-derivative jump.
For a unit u, suppose at s_0 the upper support edge of a moving fiber
has length L>0 and q(s_0)=h(s_0). Put v=h'-q'. Locally its small cap
has area L[v(s-s_0)]_++O((s-s_0)^2). Hence its right and left
derivatives are respectively L max(v,0), L min(v,0). At a lower
support event apply this rule to the complementary cap. In particular
one must not insert the full closed supporting edge into (4) without
the one-sided trace. A vertex event without an edge has no such
first-order strip term. The exact chamber formula (3) covers both.

## 3. A conditional finite bound using BOTH complementary traces

The following bound is valid for arbitrary convex bodies, not only
polygons. Fix j=0, t constant, and the scaled tilt in (2). At s=0
assume both endpoint cuts have thresholds within their closed support
intervals. Thus their upper and lower closed traces are all nonempty;
zero-volume supporting faces are allowed. Write

    p=|A intersect {u.x>=t+beta}|,
    r=|C intersect {u.x>=t-beta}|,
    P_s=F_-(s)+F_+(s), chi=s(1-s).

The endpoint thresholds at parameter s are exactly the opposed affine
interpolations of these two thresholds. Minkowski combinations of the
upper traces lie in the corresponding new upper caps. Applying planar
Brunn--Minkowski and adding the two resulting inequalities gives

    P_s>=p+r-2 chi(sqrt(p)-sqrt(r))^2.                 (7)

Apply the SAME lower-bound argument to the lower traces and subtract
it from the exact endpoint total area in (1). This gives

    P_s<=p+r+2 chi[Delta+(sqrt(a-p)-sqrt(c-r))^2].      (8)

Thus the upper bound comes from complementary lower-cap inclusion.
It is not a reversed Brunn--Minkowski assertion. The nonemptiness
hypothesis matters: an empty initial trace cannot be replaced by a
zero-volume point in a Minkowski combination. If a threshold lies
strictly outside support, use the exact cap calculus instead; (7)--(8)
are not asserted in that case.

For example let F_0 be the full original cap mass, including B, and
f=F_0/M_0. A concrete sufficient condition for this continued cap's
normalized mass not to increase is

    (1-f)Delta+(sqrt(a-p)-sqrt(c-r))^2<=0.             (9)

Indeed (8) and the constant middle cap bound its new mass by
F_0+2 chi[Delta+(sqrt(a-p)-sqrt(c-r))^2], whereas
f M_s=F_0+2 chi f Delta. This proves (9) exactly for finite s.
It is a condition on actual cap traces, not only endpoint volumes.
It can be used for every member of a finite continued cover if each
member meets the hypothesis. It alone asserts neither a center nor
that a critical cover must satisfy those inequalities.

## 4. Exact full-source depth for nested symmetric endpoints

Let K be any full-dimensional planar convex body centrally symmetric
about zero. Consider the actual source with fibers

    (1-theta)K, K, (1+theta)K, 0<=theta<1,

and write V=|K|. Its three mixed masses are (1-theta)^2 V,V,
(1+theta)^2 V. The exact normalized maximum over ALL actual candidate
points and ALL ambient halfspaces is

    D(theta)=max{(1+theta)^2/2,
                 1/2+(1-theta)^2}/(3+2theta^2).        (10)

For the lower bound at an endpoint's center, any containing cap cuts
at least half that endpoint, by symmetry. Large finite base tilts
isolate it, so its exact restricted maximum is half its area. For the
middle center, the middle cap always pays V/2. The two endpoint
thresholds are opposite. The larger endpoint contains the smaller
central symmetric copy, whose two opposite-threshold caps sum to its
whole area. Hence every nonvertical cap at the middle center pays at
least V/2+(1-theta)^2 V. A vertical containing halfspace captures the
middle and at least the smaller endpoint, which is a larger amount.

Here is a finite all-point upper cover, avoiding an unproved
fiber-centroid selector. Choose any unit u and a sufficiently large
L. The two caps

    -L z+u.x>=0, -L z-u.x>=0

each capture all the smaller endpoint, half of K, and none of the
larger endpoint. They cover every point of the middle fiber. The two
caps L(z-1) plus or minus u.x>=0 isolate and cover the upper endpoint,
each with its half-area. The two caps -L(z+1) plus or minus u.x>=0
do the same at the lower endpoint. These six actual ambient caps
cover the whole mixed source with the stated budgets. This proves
(10), including every noncentral candidate, closed boundary point,
oblique cap, and purely base-normal direction.

## 5. Full classification for arbitrary nested symmetric endpoints

The same argument works when A is contained in C, both centrally
symmetric about zero, with no homothety hypothesis. For 0<=s<=1/2,
support functions give A_s contained in B contained in C_s. Write
a_s=|A_s|, c_s=|C_s|. The exact all-point formula is

    D_s=max{c_s/2,W/2+a_s}/(a_s+c_s+W).              (11)

The lower bounds and the six isolated-cap upper cover are identical
to Section 4. If A is a proper subset of C, then a_s strictly increases
and c_s strictly decreases up to s=1/2. Indeed their support functions
are pointwise monotone and differ strictly in at least one direction
between any two distinct parameters; proper inclusion of convex bodies
strictly increases area. In particular a_s',c_s' have the corresponding
weak signs. The two normalized branches in (11) are strictly monotone,
as is also seen from their derivative numerators:

    d/ds [c_s/(2M_s)]:
                [c_s'(a_s+W)-c_s a_s']/2 <0,
    d/ds [(a_s+W/2)/M_s]:
                a_s'(c_s+W/2)-c_s'(a_s+W/2) >0.      (12)

The signs are strict in the open interval: the positive-area concave
root a_s^(1/2), increasing strictly, has positive derivative there;
the corresponding assertion for c_s follows by s ->1-s. Equivalently
this follows from the explicit area polynomials and monotonicity on
the full interval 0<=s<=1. The branch monotonicity also follows
directly from their strictly increasing/decreasing arguments, without
using derivative strictness at the final endpoint.

It follows that an interior minimum occurs if and only if

    c>W+2a.

In that case it is unique and is exactly the crossing

    c_s=W+2a_s.

The crossing exists before s=1/2 because there a_s=c_s=W. It is the
unique zero in that interval of the explicitly quadratic expression

    c-2a-W+(4a-2q-2c)s+Delta s^2.                    (13)

At this minimum the exact depth is

    (W+2a_s)/[2(2W+3a_s)] >1/4.                    (14)

If c<=W+2a, the middle branch dominates initially and thereafter, so
depth strictly increases for positive s (unless A=C). If equality
holds initially, the minimum is the boundary parameter s=0. Thus this
is an exact critical-balance classification for a nonhomothetic class,
not a numerical observation about the square example.

In fact (11) is always strictly above1/4 when the endpoint areas are
positive: if c_s>=W+2a_s the endpoint branch exceeds1/4; otherwise
the middle branch does. Consequently this entire class is separated
from the planar target2/9. At an interior minimum the active middle
caps include the ENTIRE smaller endpoint and NONE of the larger one.
Those are genuinely empty traces, so one cannot incorrectly apply
(7)--(8) to them by interpreting an empty cap as a supporting point.
The chamber calculus and finite six-cap cover do apply.

For a concrete nonhomothetic example take
A=[-1,1]x[-1/2,1/2] and C=[-2,2]x[-3,3]. Then

    a=2, c=24, W=21/2, q=8,
    a_s=2+12s+10s^2, c_s=24-32s+10s^2.

The unique strict interior minimum is at
s=(sqrt(879)-28)/10, the positive root of
19/2-56s-10s^2=0. This lies in (0,1/2), and (11)--(14)
in their preceding general form are certified by the same six actual
caps. In particular the interior-minimum obstruction is not restricted
to homothetic endpoints.

## 6. A strict interior minimum under the actual opposed flow

Take the rational initial bodies

    A=K/2, C=3K/2, B=K.

The opposed flow gives A_s=(1/2+s)K, C_s=(3/2-s)K, so
theta_s=1/2-s on 0<=s<=1/2. The two branches of (10), as functions
of theta, cross exactly once in this interval, at

    theta_*=3-sqrt(7), s_*=sqrt(7)-5/2 in (0,1/4).

Their derivatives have numerators

    d/dtheta [(3/2-2theta+theta^2)/(3+2theta^2)]
                       = (4theta^2-6)/(3+2theta^2)^2 <0,
    d/dtheta [(1+theta)^2/(2(3+2theta^2))]
                       = (3+theta-2theta^2)/(3+2theta^2)^2 >0.

The first branch is the larger one for theta<theta_*, and the second
for theta>theta_*. Therefore the FULL mixed normalized maximum has
a strict interior minimum at s_*, with exact value

    D_* =19/62-2sqrt(7)/217 >2/9.                     (15)

For an entirely explicit polyhedral example set K=[-1,1]^2. All three
fibers are positive squares, the lifted source is its full-dimensional
convex hull, and the fiber count remains three throughout the parameter
interval. The six-cap cover in Section 4 works with L=10. On
0<=s<=1/4 it also works with the requested shared scaled tilt
L_s=10(1-2s), since L_s>=5 and all continuous radii are at most3/2.
Thus the minimum is compatible with exact moving-cap budgets, not
only a stationary value tested against fixed continuous normals.

At the minimum the middle group and the larger-endpoint group have
the same critical budget; their normalized first derivatives have
opposite signs. The smaller-endpoint group is strictly slack. The
maximum of the two active budgets has a strict cusp minimum, so a
single derivative for the global maximum would be incorrect. Both
directions of the opposed flow are admissible and both increase that
maximum locally. The midpoint equality remains exact and no support
fiber is lost. This refutes universal nonincrease or an automatic
interior-to-boundary descent for this one-parameter mechanism.

It does not classify minima under arbitrary shape changes or cap
motions, and its value is separated from the requested 2/9 threshold.
In particular the existence or exclusion of a below-target local
minimum under the opposed flow is not settled by (15).
